passages.text: After David had finished speaking with Saul, the souls of Jonathan and David were knit together, and Jonathan loved him as himself.
passages.sermon:
David finished speaking with Saul.
Jonathan was Saul’s son.
Jonathan’s soul became closely bound to David’s soul.
Jonathan loved David as he loved himself.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י כְּכַלֹּתוֹ֙ לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֶל־ שָׁא֔וּל וְנֶ֙פֶשׁ֙ יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן נִקְשְׁרָ֖ה בְּנֶ֣פֶשׁ דָּוִ֑ד וַיֶּאֱהָבוֹ יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן כְּנַפְשֽׁוֹ׃

passages.text: And from that day Saul kept David with him and did not let him return to his father’s house.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
David was the son of Jesse from Bethlehem.
On that day, Saul took David with him.
Saul did not let David return to his father’s house.
passages.original: וַיִּקָּחֵ֥הוּ שָׁא֖וּל בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וְלֹ֣א נְתָנ֔וֹ לָשׁ֖וּב בֵּ֥ית אָבִֽיו׃

passages.text: Then Jonathan made a covenant with David because he loved him as himself.
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was the son of King Saul.
David was a young man who had just spoken with Saul.
Jonathan loved David as much as he loved himself.
Jonathan made a covenant with David.
Jonathan made this covenant because of his great love for David.
passages.original: וַיִּכְרֹ֧ת יְהוֹנָתָ֛ן וְדָוִ֖ד בְּרִ֑ית בְּאַהֲבָת֥וֹ אֹת֖וֹ כְּנַפְשֽׁוֹ׃

passages.text: And Jonathan removed the robe he was wearing and gave it to David, along with his tunic, his sword, his bow, and his belt.
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was the son of King Saul.
Jonathan loved David as himself.
Jonathan took off the robe he was wearing.
Jonathan gave his robe to David.
Jonathan also gave David his tunic.
Jonathan gave David his sword.
Jonathan gave David his bow.
Jonathan gave David his belt.
passages.original: וַיִּתְפַּשֵּׁ֣ט יְהוֹנָתָ֗ן אֶֽת־ הַמְּעִיל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָלָ֔יו וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֖הוּ לְדָוִ֑ד וּמַדָּ֕יו וְעַד־ חַרְבּ֥וֹ וְעַד־ קַשְׁתּ֖וֹ וְעַד־ חֲגֹרֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So David marched out and prospered in everything Saul sent him to do, and Saul set him over the men of war. And this was pleasing in the sight of all the people, and of Saul’s officers as well.
passages.sermon:
David served King Saul.
Saul sent David on many missions.
David succeeded in everything Saul asked him to do.
Saul noticed David’s success.
Saul put David in charge of the soldiers.
All the people saw this and were pleased.
Saul’s officers also approved of David.
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵ֨א דָוִ֜ד בְּכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׁלָחֶ֤נּוּ שָׁאוּל֙ יַשְׂכִּ֔יל וַיְשִׂמֵ֣הוּ שָׁא֔וּל עַ֖ל אַנְשֵׁ֣י הַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וַיִּיטַב֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י כָל־ הָעָ֔ם וְגַ֕ם בְּעֵינֵ֖י עַבְדֵ֥י שָׁאֽוּל׃פ

passages.text: As the troops were returning home after David had killed the Philistine, the women came out of all the cities of Israel to meet King Saul with singing and dancing, with joyful songs, and with tambourines and other instruments.
passages.sermon:
David killed the Philistine.
The troops returned home.
Women came out from every city in Israel.
The women wanted to meet King Saul.
The women sang and danced.
They played tambourines.
They played other instruments.
They were joyful.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י בְּבוֹאָ֗ם בְּשׁ֤וּב דָּוִד֙ מֵהַכּ֣וֹת אֶת־ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔י וַתֵּצֶ֨אנָה הַנָּשִׁ֜ים מִכָּל־ עָרֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לָשׁוּר וְהַמְּחֹל֔וֹת לִקְרַ֖את שָׁא֣וּל הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ בְּתֻפִּ֥ים בְּשִׂמְחָ֖ה וּבְשָׁלִשִֽׁים׃

passages.text: And as the women danced, they sang out: “Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands.”
passages.sermon:
Women came out from all the cities of Israel.
These women danced and played music.
They sang as they danced.
They said, “Saul has killed his thousands.”
They also said, “David has killed his tens of thousands.”
passages.original: וַֽתַּעֲנֶ֛ינָה הַנָּשִׁ֥ים הַֽמְשַׂחֲק֖וֹת וַתֹּאמַ֑רְןָ הִכָּ֤ה שָׁאוּל֙ בְּאַלְפּוֹ וְדָוִ֖ד בְּרִבְבֹתָֽיו׃

passages.text: And Saul was furious and resented this song. “They have ascribed tens of thousands to David,” he said, “but only thousands to me. What more can he have but the kingdom?”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul heard the women singing about David.
The women praised David more than Saul.
Saul became very angry.
Saul did not like what he heard.
Saul said, “They gave David credit for tens of thousands.”
Saul said, “They gave me credit for only thousands.”
Saul said, “What else can David get but the kingdom?”
passages.original: וַיִּ֨חַר לְשָׁא֜וּל מְאֹ֗ד וַיֵּ֤רַע בְּעֵינָיו֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר נָתְנ֤וּ לְדָוִד֙ רְבָב֔וֹת וְלִ֥י נָתְנ֖וּ הָאֲלָפִ֑ים וְע֥וֹד ל֖וֹ אַ֥ךְ הַמְּלוּכָֽה׃

passages.text: And from that day forward Saul kept a jealous eye on David.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
David was a young man who served Saul.
Saul became jealous of David.
This happened after the women praised David more than Saul.
From that day on, Saul watched David with jealousy.
Saul continued to be jealous of David from that time forward.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֥י שָׁא֖וּל עָוֹן אֶת־ דָּוִ֑ד מֵהַיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא וָהָֽלְאָה׃ס

passages.text: The next day a spirit of distress sent from God came upon Saul, and he prophesied inside the house while David played the harp as usual. Now Saul was holding a spear, and he hurled it, thinking, “I will pin David to the wall.” But David eluded him twice.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
David was a young man who served Saul.
The next day, God sent an evil spirit to Saul.
This spirit troubled Saul deeply.
Saul began to prophesy inside his house.
David played the harp with his hand.
David did this every day to help Saul.
Saul held a spear in his hand.
Saul threw the spear.
Saul said, “I will strike David and pin him to the wall.”
David escaped from Saul two times.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י מִֽמָּחֳרָ֗ת וַתִּצְלַ֣ח רוּחַ֩ אֱלֹהִ֨ים׀ רָעָ֤ה׀ אֶל־ שָׁאוּל֙ וַיִּתְנַבֵּ֣א בְתוֹךְ־ הַבַּ֔יִת וְדָוִ֛ד מְנַגֵּ֥ן בְּיָד֖וֹ כְּי֣וֹם׀ בְּי֑וֹם וְהַחֲנִ֖ית בְּיַד־ שָׁאֽוּל׃ וַיָּ֤טֶל שָׁאוּל֙ אֶֽת־ הַחֲנִ֔ית וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אַכֶּ֥ה בְדָוִ֖ד וּבַקִּ֑יר וַיִּסֹּ֥ב דָּוִ֛ד מִפָּנָ֖יו פַּעֲמָֽיִם׃

passages.text: So Saul was afraid of David, because the LORD was with David but had departed from Saul.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
David was a young man who served Saul.
The LORD was with David.
The LORD had left Saul.
Saul saw that the LORD was with David.
Saul became afraid of David.
passages.original: וַיִּרָ֥א שָׁא֖וּל מִלִּפְנֵ֣י דָוִ֑ד כִּֽי־ הָיָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וּמֵעִ֥ם שָׁא֖וּל סָֽר׃

passages.text: Therefore Saul sent David away and gave him command of a thousand men. David led the troops out to battle and back, and he continued to prosper in all his ways, because the LORD was with him.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul became afraid of David.
Saul sent David away from him.
Saul made David a commander over a thousand men.
David led his men out to battle.
David brought his men back safely.
David succeeded in everything he did.
The LORD was with David.
passages.original: וַיְסִרֵ֤הוּ שָׁאוּל֙ מֵֽעִמּ֔וֹ וַיְשִׂמֵ֥הוּ ל֖וֹ שַׂר־ אָ֑לֶף וַיֵּצֵ֥א וַיָּבֹ֖א לִפְנֵ֥י הָעָֽם׃פ וַיְהִ֥י דָוִ֛ד לְכָל־ דְּרָכָ֖ו מַשְׂכִּ֑יל וַֽיהוָ֖ה עִמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: When Saul saw that David was very successful, he was afraid of him.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
David was a young man who served Saul.
The LORD was with David.
David succeeded in everything he did.
Saul saw that David was very successful.
Saul became afraid of David.
passages.original: וַיַּ֣רְא שָׁא֔וּל אֲשֶׁר־ ה֖וּא מַשְׂכִּ֣יל מְאֹ֑ד וַיָּ֖גָר מִפָּנָֽיו׃

passages.text: But all Israel and Judah loved David, because he was leading them out to battle and back.
passages.sermon:
All the people of Israel loved David.
All the people of Judah loved David.
David led the people out to battle.
David brought the people back from battle.
The people loved David because he led them.
passages.original: וְכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וִיהוּדָ֔ה אֹהֵ֖ב אֶת־ דָּוִ֑ד כִּֽי־ ה֛וּא יוֹצֵ֥א וָבָ֖א לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃פ

passages.text: Then Saul said to David, “Here is my older daughter Merab. I will give her to you in marriage. Only be valiant for me and fight the LORD’s battles.” But Saul was thinking, “I need not raise my hand against him; let the hand of the Philistines be against him.”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
David was a young man who was very successful in battle.
Saul spoke to David.
Saul said, “Here is my older daughter, Merab.
I will give Merab to you as a wife.
But you must be brave for me.
You must fight the LORD’s battles.”
Saul thought something in his heart.
Saul thought, “I do not need to harm David myself.
Let the Philistines harm him instead.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֜וּל אֶל־ דָּוִ֗ד הִנֵּה֩ בִתִּ֨י הַגְּדוֹלָ֤ה מֵרַב֙ אֹתָהּ֙ אֶתֶּן־ לְךָ֣ לְאִשָּׁ֔ה אַ֚ךְ הֱיֵה־ לִּ֣י לְבֶן־ חַ֔יִל וְהִלָּחֵ֖ם מִלְחֲמ֣וֹת יְהוָ֑ה וְשָׁא֣וּל אָמַ֗ר אַל־ תְּהִ֤י יָדִי֙ בּ֔וֹ וּתְהִי־ ב֖וֹ יַד־ פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃ס

passages.text: And David said to Saul, “Who am I, and what is my family or my father’s clan in Israel, that I should become the son-in-law of the king?”
passages.sermon:
David was a young man from Israel.
David spoke to Saul, the king of Israel.
David said, “Who am I?”
David said, “What is my life?”
David said, “What is my father’s family in Israel?”
David said, “Why should I become the king’s son-in-law?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד אֶל־ שָׁא֗וּל מִ֤י אָֽנֹכִי֙ וּמִ֣י חַיַּ֔י מִשְׁפַּ֥חַת אָבִ֖י בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּֽי־ אֶהְיֶ֥ה חָתָ֖ן לַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: So when it was time to give Saul’s daughter Merab to David, she was given in marriage to Adriel of Meholah.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Merab was Saul’s older daughter.
Saul promised to give Merab to David as a wife.
The time came to give Merab to David.
Saul did not give Merab to David.
Saul gave Merab to Adriel of Meholah as a wife.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י בְּעֵ֥ת תֵּ֛ת אֶת־ מֵרַ֥ב בַּת־ שָׁא֖וּל לְדָוִ֑ד וְהִ֧יא נִתְּנָ֛ה לְעַדְרִיאֵ֥ל הַמְּחֹלָתִ֖י לְאִשָּֽׁה׃

passages.text: Now Saul’s daughter Michal loved David, and when this was reported to Saul, it pleased him.
passages.sermon:
Michal was Saul’s daughter.
Michal loved David.
People told Saul that Michal loved David.
Saul felt pleased when he heard this.
passages.original: וַתֶּאֱהַ֛ב מִיכַ֥ל בַּת־ שָׁא֖וּל אֶת־ דָּוִ֑ד וַיַּגִּ֣דוּ לְשָׁא֔וּל וַיִּשַׁ֥ר הַדָּבָ֖ר בְּעֵינָֽיו׃

passages.text: “I will give her to David,” Saul thought, “so that she may be a snare to him, and the hand of the Philistines may be against him.” So Saul said to David, “For a second time now you can be my son-in-law.”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul wanted to give his daughter to David.
Saul thought, "I will give her to David."
Saul wanted her to be a snare to David.
Saul wanted the Philistines to attack David.
Saul said to David, "For the second time, you can become my son-in-law today."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֜וּל אֶתְּנֶ֤נָּה לּוֹ֙ וּתְהִי־ ל֣וֹ לְמוֹקֵ֔שׁ וּתְהִי־ ב֖וֹ יַד־ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שָׁאוּל֙ אֶל־ דָּוִ֔ד בִּשְׁתַּ֛יִם תִּתְחַתֵּ֥ן בִּ֖י הַיּֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Then Saul ordered his servants, “Speak to David privately and tell him, ‘Behold, the king is pleased with you, and all his servants love you. Now therefore, become his son-in-law.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul gave a command to his servants.
He told them to speak to David in secret.
Saul said, “Tell David this message.”
“The king is pleased with you.”
“All the king’s servants love you.”
“Now, become the king’s son-in-law.”
passages.original: וַיְצַ֨ו שָׁא֜וּל אֶת־ עֲבָדָ֗ו דַּבְּר֨וּ אֶל־ דָּוִ֤ד בַּלָּט֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִנֵּ֨ה חָפֵ֤ץ בְּךָ֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְכָל־ עֲבָדָ֖יו אֲהֵב֑וּךָ וְעַתָּ֖ה הִתְחַתֵּ֥ן בַּמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: But when Saul’s servants relayed these words to David, he replied, “Does it seem trivial in your sight to be the son-in-law of the king? I am a poor man and lightly esteemed.”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul wanted David to marry his daughter.
Saul’s servants spoke to David.
They told David what Saul had said.
David listened to the servants.
David replied to them.
David said, “Is it a small thing to become the king’s son-in-law?”
David said, “I am a poor man.”
David said, “I am not highly regarded.”
passages.original: וַֽיְדַבְּר֞וּ עַבְדֵ֤י שָׁאוּל֙ בְּאָזְנֵ֣י דָוִ֔ד אֶת־ הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗ד הַֽנְקַלָּ֤ה בְעֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ הִתְחַתֵּ֣ן בַּמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְאָנֹכִ֖י אִֽישׁ־ רָ֥שׁ וְנִקְלֶֽה׃

passages.text: And the servants told Saul what David had said.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
David was a young man in Saul’s court.
Saul’s servants spoke to David.
David answered the servants.
The servants went to Saul.
The servants told Saul David’s exact words.
passages.original: וַיַּגִּ֜דוּ עַבְדֵ֥י שָׁא֛וּל ל֖וֹ לֵאמֹ֑ר כַּדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה דִּבֶּ֥ר דָּוִֽד׃פ

passages.text: Saul replied, “Say to David, ‘The king desires no other dowry but a hundred Philistine foreskins as revenge on his enemies.’ ” But Saul intended to cause David’s death at the hands of the Philistines.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul spoke to his servants.
He told them to speak to David.
Saul said, “Tell David this.”
“The king does not want any other dowry.”
“He wants one hundred Philistine foreskins.”
“The king wants this as revenge on his enemies.”
Saul planned to harm David.
Saul hoped the Philistines would kill David.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֜וּל כֹּֽה־ תֹאמְר֣וּ לְדָוִ֗ד אֵֽין־ חֵ֤פֶץ לַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ בְּמֹ֔הַר כִּ֗י בְּמֵאָה֙ עָרְל֣וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים לְהִנָּקֵ֖ם בְּאֹיְבֵ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְשָׁא֣וּל חָשַׁ֔ב לְהַפִּ֥יל אֶת־ דָּוִ֖ד בְּיַד־ פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

passages.text: When the servants reported these terms to David, he was pleased to become the king’s son-in-law. Before the wedding day arrived, David and his men went out and killed two hundred Philistines. He brought their foreskins and presented them as payment in full to become the king’s son-in-law. Then Saul gave his daughter Michal to David in marriage.
passages.sermon:
David was a young man in Israel.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul’s servants spoke to David.
They told David what Saul had said.
Saul wanted David to become his son-in-law.
David heard these words.
David was pleased to marry the king’s daughter.
The wedding day had not yet come.
David gathered his men.
David and his men went out to fight the Philistines.
David and his men killed two hundred Philistines.
David took the foreskins of the Philistines.
David brought the foreskins to Saul.
David gave the foreskins to Saul as the full payment.
David did this to become the king’s son-in-law.
Saul gave his daughter Michal to David in marriage.
passages.original: וַיַּגִּ֨דוּ עֲבָדָ֤יו לְדָוִד֙ אֶת־ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה וַיִּשַׁ֤ר הַדָּבָר֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י דָוִ֔ד לְהִתְחַתֵּ֖ן בַּמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְלֹ֥א מָלְא֖וּ הַיָּמִֽים׃ וַיָּ֨קָם דָּוִ֜ד וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ׀ ה֣וּא וַאֲנָשָׁ֗יו וַיַּ֣ךְ בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּים֮ מָאתַ֣יִם אִישׁ֒ וַיָּבֵ֤א דָוִד֙ אֶת־ עָרְלֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם וַיְמַלְא֣וּם לַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לְהִתְחַתֵּ֖ן בַּמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיִּתֶּן־ ל֥וֹ שָׁא֛וּל אֶת־ מִיכַ֥ל בִּתּ֖וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃ס

passages.text: When Saul realized that the LORD was with David and that his daughter Michal loved David, he grew even more afraid of David. So from then on Saul was David’s enemy.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
David was a young man chosen by God.
The LORD was with David.
Michal was Saul’s daughter.
Michal loved David.
Saul saw that the LORD was with David.
Saul knew that Michal loved David.
Saul became more afraid of David.
Saul became David’s enemy.
Saul remained David’s enemy for the rest of his life.
passages.original: וַיַּ֤רְא שָׁאוּל֙ וַיֵּ֔דַע כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה עִם־ דָּוִ֑ד וּמִיכַ֥ל בַּת־ שָׁא֖וּל אֲהֵבַֽתְהוּ׃ וַיֹּ֣אסֶף שָׁא֗וּל לֵרֹ֛א מִפְּנֵ֥י דָוִ֖ד ע֑וֹד וַיְהִ֥י שָׁא֛וּל אֹיֵ֥ב אֶת־ דָּוִ֖ד כָּל־ הַיָּמִֽים׃ס

passages.text: Every time the Philistine commanders came out for battle, David was more successful than all of Saul’s officers, so that his name was highly esteemed.
passages.sermon:
David was a servant of King Saul.
Philistine commanders often came out for battle.
Each time they came out, David went to fight.
David succeeded more than all of Saul’s other officers.
People respected David’s name very much.
passages.original: וַיֵּצְא֖וּ שָׂרֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיְהִ֣י׀ מִדֵּ֣י צֵאתָ֗ם שָׂכַ֤ל דָּוִד֙ מִכֹּל֙ עַבְדֵ֣י שָׁא֔וּל וַיִּיקַ֥ר שְׁמ֖וֹ מְאֹֽד׃ס
